title: Delta-Map Belief Updates for Stable Spatial Revision in Vision-Language Models

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable VLMs to maintain and revise spatial beliefs over time without wasteful and error-prone full cognitive-map regeneration. This objective is not directly covered by any prior paper. While several papers address belief revision (e.g., [2], [6], [8], [13], [30], [31]), they focus on general belief revision or truth maintenance systems rather than the specific problem of spatial belief maintenance in VLMs. Papers on dialogue state tracking ([18], [22], [29], [32], [34]) involve belief updates but are limited to dialogue systems and do not address spatial reasoning or cognitive-map regeneration. No prior paper explicitly targets the same problem-class level objective.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a delta-map belief update interface that treats cognitive maps (structured JSON) as external state and updates them through sparse delta operations with explicit preserve/overwrite rules. This mechanism is substantively equivalent to [19] (JSON Patch), which defines a JSON document structure for expressing a sequence of operations to apply to a JSON document, including sparse updates. Additionally, [12] (JSON Merge Patch) and [11] (JSON Whisperer) describe similar mechanisms for efficient JSON editing using patch-based approaches. These papers cover the same underlying primitive of sparse delta-based updates with explicit modification rules, even though their application domains differ.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses the Theory of Space benchmark to show that providing prior map context improves false-belief identification F1 by +16.7 percentage points over scratch regeneration. This evaluation design is covered by [20] (Do Language Models Have Beliefs?), which uses LLMs as judges to evaluate belief-related tasks, and [11] (JSON Whisperer), which evaluates patch-based editing frameworks using JSON-based benchmarks. Both papers employ similar evaluation designs involving task-specific benchmarks and metrics to validate belief-related updates. The specific benchmark instance (Theory of Space) is new, but the evaluation design itself is not.

### Domain
The domain is spatial reasoning in vision-language models. Spatial reasoning is a well-established application area, and prior papers such as [20] (Do Language Models Have Beliefs?) and [18] (Dialogue State Tracking) address belief-related reasoning tasks in language models. While these papers do not focus specifically on spatial reasoning, they operate within the broader domain of reasoning tasks in VLMs and dialogue systems. Thus, the domain is covered.
